correctness.rationale: The unit ball is the symmetric edge polytope. A tight-graph rank criterion proves all polar vertices are two-level cuts or one special three-level pair. Convexity of A->y^TA^{-1}y and symmetry permit restricting to a two-eigenspace invariant form without losing the optimum. Every graph edge has squared projection lengths one in both summands. Exact rational energies for all polar vertex types give the global upper bounds. Explicit connected-tight cuts and a special vertex yield lower bounds k for k>=4 (even/odd separate) and 10/3 for k=3; k=2 yields 3. Independently executable rational checker enumerates all vertices and confirms maxima for k=2..8; no extrapolation from checks is used.

originality.rationale: Direct statement-and-implication comparison to four primary sources, numerous mathematical research-record queries, and the accessible 87-entry private claim ledger found no theorem computing Euclidean Banach--Mazur distances of matching-deleted complete graph free spaces for every k. Existing complete-multipartite facet counts are correctly attributed, and the k=2 case is explicitly prior known. Distinct infinite k>=4 formula and the anisotropic k=3 boundary are supported by new group-symmetry optimization and exact contact certificates. Residual risk: unindexed earlier treatment, and incomplete pagewise scrutiny of unrelated sections of broad surveys.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently named result may already optimize Hilbert distortion for the same family.
Only relevant identified primary sections were inspected; this is not an exhaustive review of all literature or all pages of survey articles.
The known k=2 case is included as a boundary consistency statement, not as the novel contribution.

value.rationale: The Euclidean Banach--Mazur distance is a basic quantitative Hilbertian invariant of finite metric transportation spaces. Exact values on the complete graph minus a perfect matching were not obtainable from known facet tables without a nontrivial ellipsoid optimization. The full infinite-family classification finds an unexpected k=3 anisotropic regime and a sharp canonical-Euclidean stabilization from k=4, with asymptotic ratio 1/sqrt2 to dimension-maximal distortion. This is a structural, natural family-wide fact rather than a small incremental parameter sample.
